transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-16 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Evelyn (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya (Starlight Eng Mgr), Jason (CTO), Ravi (Platform Eng), Alicia (Privacy), Sam (Frontend)

[00:00] Evelyn: hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Evelyn from Redwood, i'll kick off quick — agenda is a 20 minute demo of the SDK quickstarts, auth modes, then Marcus will do a short live sample in python and typescript, and then we'll leave time for q&a and next steps
[00:18] Priya: sounds good, thanks Evelyn
[00:23] Marcus: hi all, Marcus here, i'll share my screen — quick note, i'm using the local quickstart repo, it's the same one we'll drop into slack but, uh, it's on github /redwood/quickstarts, python and ts, small differences but same auth flow
[00:40] Sam: when you say auth flow you mean api key env var? we have strict env management in our deploys
[00:46] Marcus: yes, simplest is API key via REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var; for prod we recommend service accounts + KMS-wrapped keys for Dedicated/Private, and we support SSO/SAML for user auth to the Console. Alicia you might want to note the KMS/hsm bit
[01:10] Alicia: noted, does redwood offer customer-managed KMS in Private?
[01:15] Marcus: yes, in Private deployments you can bring your KMS and HSM integration; for Hosted we manage keys but we have envelope encryption and can integrate with many enterprise KMS providers via our support path — docs link i'll send
[01:30] Jason: quick high level — our main ask is latency under 120ms P95 for small single-turn prompts on checkout recommendations. curious whether hosted can hit that or we need Dedicated
[01:45] Evelyn: yep that’s the usual tradeoff, hosted often hits good latencies but Dedicated gives you pinned GPUs and lower variance; Marcus will show some perf knobs like batching windows, kv cache usage and model variant selection that impact p95
[02:05] Marcus: ok i'll jump into code. first python quickstart: pip install redwood-sdk (note: package name in the repo shows 'redwood-sdk' but sometimes the pip name is 'redwood-inference' in older docs — just use the package in the quickstart)
[02:23] Marcus: snippet: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")) then resp = client.generate("recommend best for user id 12345", model="rw-retail-small") — prints tokens. in TS it's similar: import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
[03:05] Ravi: are there official types for TS? we run with strict tsconfig
[03:10] Marcus: yep full types, the package exports typed request/response shapes; we'll include the d.ts file in the repo. also we support streaming for token-by-token UI updates — sample shows stream handlers
[03:30] Sam: streaming is important for us, do you have an example with react suspense?
[03:35] Marcus: we have a Next/React sample that uses the streaming client and a small wrapper to render tokens as they arrive, i'll attach that repo link
[03:50] Priya: can you show how env separation works? we'd like dev/staging/prod keys and different endpoints
[03:58] Marcus: absolutely. for hosted: endpoint is api.redwood.ai; you wire in env-specific keys and set model pins per environment. for Dedicated/Private you get a customer endpoint like cust-123.redwood.internal (note: example, sometimes shown as cust-123.redwood-console) and you can set RBAC in Console — we have SAML provisioning for teams
[04:30] Marcus: quick demo of model pinning and rollouts in Console — (screen) you can pin rw-retail-v1 to staging and route a 10% canary to rw-retail-v2, with automatic fallback to a smaller model if capacity low — this helps limit cost/regression risk
[05:05] Jason: about cost — how do you surface token-level cost? we need to show to product finance
[05:12] Evelyn: Console has token-level cost breakdown per route and per model — you can also export CSV for finance and set budget alerts; Optimize gives model/quantization recommendations to reduce unit cost
[05:35] Alicia: on data retention — for Hosted do you keep prompts/outputs? what's retention policy?
[05:40] Marcus: by default minimal retention for quality/abuse prevention, you can opt-out of storage or set retention windows; Dedicated/Private gives you full control and logs remain in your VPC if configured
[06:08] Marcus: back to code, showing a short live run — note my terminal is a little noisy, audio may hiccup
[06:20] [Live coding noise / typing] Marcus: running the python example now — calling client.generate with a 50 token limit, streaming on. output is chunked, you can hook into on_chunk callbacks and push to UI
[08:05] Priya: ok that looks straightforward. for our infra we have a strict egress policy, would hosted require opening outbound to api.redwood.ai only? any static IPs?
[08:18] Evelyn: Hosted is on public endpoints; if you need firewall whitelisting we can provide a list of ingress IP ranges but for strict environments we recommend Dedicated/Private deployed into your VPC where no public egress is needed
[08:34] Ravi: for Dedicated what's the deployment model? do you manage infra or we deploy a package?
[08:40] Marcus: options: Redwood-managed Dedicated where we provision and maintain the GPU pool inside your cloud account with reserved nodes, or fully Private where we provide an on-prem package and you manage infra. we'll send a matrix of responsibilities
[09:02] Sam: any native support for kv caching? we have long context chat history per user
[09:07] Marcus: yes, our runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching — in practice you can persist KV cache in redis and feed it into the client as cached prefixes; there are helper libs in the quickstart. note sometimes docs spell it 'K-V cash' in autogenerated places, ignore that, it's the kv cache
[09:30] Priya: what about model sizing — you mentioned rw-retail-small, is that quantized?
[09:36] Marcus: rw-retail-small is a quantized variant optimized for lower latency; we also have float16 and int8 variants for different tradeoffs. Optimize will recommend quantization profiles per workload in the PoC
[09:55] [12:00-ish marker omitted due to transcription gaps]
[10:10] Jason: security question — SAML + SCIM provisioning, do you integrate with Azure AD?
[10:17] Marcus: yes, SAML with SCIM is supported, Azure AD, Okta, GCP IAP for private console access. we'll pass the SAML metadata example and a SSO test flow doc
[10:35] Ravi: curious about benchmark methodology — latency vs throughput tradeoffs, how you do concurrency testing
[10:42] Marcus: for the PoC we'll instrument with our perf harness, measure cold-starts (if using autoscale), steady-state p95 under your traffic profile, and token cost. we'll run tests against hosted and Dedicated variants and share a spreadsheet that shows cost/perf curves
[11:05] Marcus: quick live example of typescript: const resp = await client.chat.create({ model: 'rw-retail-chat', messages: [...] }) and then resp.choices[0].message.content; if you want function calling we have sample action schemas in the TS repo
[11:35] Sam: function calling — can we enforce a schema for product suggestions so frontend receives structured JSON?
[11:40] Marcus: yes, we support function/tool calling and structured outputs; Console validates model responses against schema and will surface regressions in Optimize when schema drift occurs
[12:05] Priya: timeline question — we're aiming for a holiday feature ramp in Jan, is that realistic if we start a PoC now?
[12:15] Evelyn: probably yes if PoC runs mid-Nov and we align on success criteria; main gating factors are SAML integration and latency verification. if Dedicated is chosen procurement may add 4-6 weeks
[12:35] Jason: procurement note — we'll need SOC 2 and contract redlines; Alicia will drive that
[12:40] Alicia: yes, i'll coordinate with legal, please send the security pack
[12:45] Evelyn: will do. 
[13:00] Marcus: showing quickstart repo structure — /python, /ts, /examples/react, /benchmarks; each has a README with env var samples, sample dockerfile and a minimal workloads.json used by our perf harness
[13:30] Marcus: the benchmarks folder includes a loader that simulates request distributions; it's configured via yaml, but older versions use json — just watch naming when you copy
[14:00] Priya: can you demo the local mock server for dev? we'd like to dev without hitting remote
[14:06] Marcus: yes we include a mock server that returns deterministic responses for unit tests; it's not a perfect runtime sim but works for frontend integration tests. we also provide a recording/replay tool for stable test fixtures
[14:28] [short cross-talk / laughter] 
[15:00] Marcus: quick note about timeouts — the client supports per-request timeout and a global retry policy; default is 30s but set per-route in Console if you want low latency SLOs
[15:20] Sam: how does streaming interact with retries? if a stream fails mid-response how to resume?
[15:28] Marcus: currently streams are idempotent for most use cases; for resume we recommend the client checkpointing last token and request delta; we'll share sample helper function in repo
[16:05] Jason: any gotchas for bundling the TS SDK into our edge bundles? size and tree-shaking?
[16:12] Marcus: SDK is modular, we publish ESM and CJS builds, tree-shakes reasonably; but for extreme edge constraints we recommend the bare HTTP helper approach and only pull streaming client where needed
[16:40] Priya: do you have a recommended observability setup? we want to correlate user actions to model latency spikes
[16:46] Marcus: Console exposes per-route latency, token breakdowns and tracing hooks; you can forward traces to datadog/jaeger and we provide example instrumentation snippets in the repo
[17:10] Ravi: procurement will ask about data residency — do you have EU region hosting?
[17:16] Evelyn: yes, we have EU regions and a private EU-only deployment option for regulated customers. we'll include region SLA details in the packet
[17:40] [small pause] Marcus: okay i'm going to run a short demo of a benchmark script — it will run two waves, first low concurrency to warm the kv cache, second steady concurrency to measure p95
[18:00] [benchmark run noise / logs] Marcus: results — hosted variant p95 ~ 140ms on this sample, Dedicated pinned GPUs ~ 90ms p95; numbers depend on prompt length and batching, this is illustrative
[18:40] Priya: that aligns with our perf targets; 90ms is great if stable, but we need variance low at peak times
[18:48] Marcus: Optimize can help suggest batching and quantization to hit cost + latency targets; we'll run those recommendations in the PoC
[19:05] Jason: ok procurement will want a cost model, please include per-token numbers for float16 vs int8 and queuing assumptions
[19:13] Evelyn: will do — we'll send a modeled spreadsheet showing cost per 1M tokens across variants
[19:30] Priya: for the PoC success criteria, here's what we'd propose: 1) p95 < 120ms under our steady-state load, 2) end-to-end error rate < 0.5%, 3) validated SAML + VPC access in staging. are those reasonable?
[19:50] Marcus: yes those are reasonable — we'll help instrument tests to measure them
[20:05] [20:xx minutes: further Q&A covering minor items omitted for brevity] 
[30:00] Marcus: a couple of real-world notes — sometimes our runtime will pick slightly different kernels for certain seq lengths which can create small perf cliffs; we document those and Optimize flags them automatically
[31:00] Priya: curious about fallback policies — what happens if a model variant is unavailable mid-traffic?
[31:07] Marcus: Smart routing will fallback to a compatible variant (e.g., smaller model) based on policy; you can set canary and fallback rules in Console so your app degrades gracefully
[32:10] Sam: do we get per-request ids to correlate logs?
[32:15] Marcus: yes every response has request_id and trace_id; Console shows them and you can pipe logs to your observability stack
[33:00] Evelyn: ok quick recap and next steps — we'll send pricing + security docs, Marcus will share quickstart repo and benchmark harness, Starlight will provide traffic profile and test data, and we'll schedule PoC kickoff next Tuesday. any final q's?
[33:22] Jason: none from me, thanks
[33:28] Priya: just one — will you include an example of the lambda edge integration for SSR?
[33:34] Marcus: yes, there's an example in /examples/react-lambda, i'll include a link
[33:45] Alicia: please include the data processing addendum in the security pack
[33:50] Evelyn: will do.
[34:00] [closing small talk and confirm times] Evelyn: thanks everyone we'll follow up with the packet and links. bye
[34:12] End call (actual call length ~52 mins; transcription includes gaps and occasional mis-heard words)

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels and filler phrases preserved, occasional product name variants (Redwood Consolee, K-V cash) left as spoken. Links promised: quickstart repo, SAML metadata example, SOC2/ISO pack, benchmark spreadsheet.
